take: A golf brand that sells a A$16,000 sculpture is either doing a bit or means it. Found means it. The Melbourne store carries thirty-five art objects alongside the clothes — stools, a dartboard, a bench, a carved textile by Damien Wright and Tony Birch titled Country-club — against thirty apparel pieces. The line about activating golf as creative culture, which every brand writes, is here just a description of the inventory.

The clothes are quieter than the art suggests. The Shiz Knit and Shiz Vest are cricket-jumper shapes with a single red tab; the 1/4 Zip puts FOUND down the spine. It was born in Cape Town, designed in London, and is now made back in Cape Town and sold out of Melbourne — a longer way round than most brands take to a polo. If you want golf clothes that read as design-studio rather than pro-shop, the A$85 Tee Box is the cheapest way in. Move quickly on anything you like: all eight cap colourways are already gone.
_match_note: These MUST be the display names build-found-golf.py writes into .product-brand, not the ALL-CAPS Shopify titles. The template matches against the rendered page, and it refuses the whole build if a match string finds nothing — which is how the first attempt failed on 'BOX PAR TEE'.

related.why: The other Australian brand on the site that treats the graphic as the point.
Sydney, and the same refusal to pick one sport.
Design-led golf clothing with an art-school accent.
London, and the same habit of dressing golf as everyday clothing.
